title: Migrate your data
question: Where are your passwords or other data coming from?
noMatch: No match. Choose CSV file: most exports work.
steps_chrome: In Chrome, open Settings › Autofill and passwords › Google Password Manager › Settings, choose Export passwords and save the CSV file.
steps_safari: In Safari on a Mac, choose File › Export › Passwords and save the CSV file.
steps_firefox: In Firefox, open about:logins, click the ••• menu, choose Export Passwords and save the CSV file.
steps_edge: In Edge, open Settings › Passwords, click ••• › Export passwords and save the CSV file.
steps_brave: In Brave, open brave://password-manager/settings, choose Export passwords and save the CSV file.
steps_other_browser: Most browsers export saved passwords as a CSV file from their password settings. Export it, then choose the file below.
steps_bitwarden: In the Bitwarden web vault or app, open Tools › Export vault and choose the .json format (not “.json (Encrypted)”): it keeps cards, identities, notes, SSH keys, custom fields and folders. CSV keeps logins and notes only.
steps_lastpass: In the LastPass extension or web vault, open Advanced options › Export and save the CSV file.
steps_apple_passwords: On a Mac, open the Passwords app, choose File › Export All Passwords and save the CSV file.
steps_dashlane: In Dashlane, open Settings › Export data › Export to CSV, then choose credentials.csv from the exported folder.
steps_keepass: Choose your .kdbx database directly and type its master password below (add the key file if the database uses one). Or, in KeePass, choose File › Export › KeePass CSV (1.x).
steps_keepassxc: Choose your .kdbx database directly and type its password below (add the key file if the database uses one; hardware keys are not supported). Or, in KeePassXC, choose Database › Export › CSV File.
steps_roboform: In RoboForm, open Options › Account & Data › Export, choose CSV and save the file.
steps_onepassword: In the 1Password app, choose File › Export, pick the account and the 1PUX format (it keeps identities, cards, notes, sections and tags; CSV keeps logins only), then choose the file here.
steps_proton_pass: In Proton Pass, open Settings › Export, choose CSV and save the file.
steps_nordpass: In NordPass, open Settings › Export items and save the CSV file.
steps_other_manager: Export your data as a CSV file from your password manager's settings. Columns such as name, url, username and password are recognised.
steps_spreadsheet: Save the spreadsheet as CSV with a first row of column names: name, url, username, password, notes.
steps_csv: Choose any CSV file with columns such as name, url, username, password, notes, totp and tags.
keeps: Folders become tags, favorites stay favorites and notes-only entries become secure notes.
chooseExport: Choose the export file and import…
keepassPassword: KeePass database password (only to open the file; not stored)
steps_cxf: Choose a CXF file (the standard credential exchange format, .json). It brings logins with their passkeys and one-time passwords, cards, notes and every other field. Attached files and SSH private keys are not in such files.
